content: 1. The dose of rotrectinib should be adjusted after discontinuation of a CYP3A4 inducer for 3-5 half-lives. 2. Both efavirenz and lefamulin prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should either be avoided or replaced with an alternative. 3. Efavirenz reduces the plasma levels or efficacy of lemborexant by altering CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lenacapavir through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Lenacapavir should not be co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 6. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of leniolisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Both efavirenz and lenvatinib increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of letermovir through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Co-administration of letermovir with UGT1A1/3 inducers is not recommended. 10. Both efavirenz and lofexidine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Lorlatinib reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lovastatin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Efavirenz may interfere with the manufacturing of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. 15. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce serum concentrations and antimalarial efficacy. 17. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of macimorelin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may lead to false-positive test results. Both efavirenz and macimorelin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of macitentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 20. Both efavirenz and methadone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Efavirenz increases the levels of methylergonovine by reducing its metabolism, potentially leading to vasospasm and ischemia. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Efavirenz and intranasal metoclopramide may enhance each other's effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug depending on the clinical importance. 23. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of midostaurin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of mifepristone. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Both efavirenz and moxifloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of naloxegol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 27. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of nateglinide by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of nefazodone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 30. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Chronic use of strong CYP3A4 inducers with netupitant is not recommended. 31. Nevirapine reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended due to increased adverse reactions without improved efficacy. 32. Both efavirenz and nilotinib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of nirogacestat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of olaparib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A inducers is unavoidable, monitor for reduced efficacy. 37. Both efavirenz and intranasal olopatadine increase sedation, leading to additive CNS depression and impaired psychomotor performance. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of olutasidenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers decrease olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. 39. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Both efavirenz and ondansetron prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of osimertinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Both efavirenz and oxaliplatin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Both efavirenz and ozanimod prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of palovarotene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Both efavirenz and panobinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Both efavirenz and pazopanib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of pemigatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Both efavirenz and pentamidine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of perampanel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of pexidartinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pexidartinib may cause hepatotoxicity; avoid co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents. 52. Both efavirenz and pimavanserin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Both efavirenz and pimozide prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 54. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, adjust the pirtobrutinib dose accordingly. 55. Both efavirenz and pitolisant prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of pomalidomide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Both efavirenz and ponesimod prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of pralsetinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of co-administration. Resume the previous dose 14 days after discontinuing the inducer. 59. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of praziquantel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of pretomanid by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid regimens are associated with hepatotoxicity; avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents. 61. Both efavirenz and procainamide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Both efavirenz and propafenone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Both efavirenz and quetiapine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 64. Both efavirenz and quinidine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Both efavirenz and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of quizartinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 67. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ranolazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 68. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of regorafenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease regorafenib levels but increase exposure to its active metabolite M-5. 69. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 70. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of rifabutin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Both efavirenz and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of rimegepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 73. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of ripretinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor may decrease systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite, potentially reducing adverse reactions. 74. Both efavirenz and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 75. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of rolapitant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Long-term co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may significantly reduce rolapitant efficacy. 76. Both efavirenz and ropeginterferon alfa-2b may increase neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor for excessive CNS toxicity. 77. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of selpercatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 78. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of selumetinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 79. Both efavirenz and sevoflurane prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 80. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of silodosin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 81. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of siponimod by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with drugs causing moderate CYP2C9 and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibition is not recommended. 82. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of sirolimus by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 83. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Velpatasvir is a substrate of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4, and moderate-to-potent inducers of these enzymes may significantly reduce its plasma concentrations and therapeutic effect. 84. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of sonidegib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 85. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of sorafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
